extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in algebraic topology; mathematicians studying cohomology and Poincaré duality
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and understanding Poincaré duality for manifolds: constructing fundamental classes, defining cap product and cohomology with compact supports, and proving the duality isomorphisms for closed and noncompact R-orientable n-manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientability over a coefficient ring R
rubrics_metrics.description: A manifold is R-orientable if there is a continuous choice of generator in the local top-dimensional homology H_n(M||x;R) at each x. An orientable manifold is R-orientable for all R; a nonorientable manifold is R-orientable iff R contains a unit of order 2 (equivalently 2 = 0 in R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: every manifold is Z2-orientable; in practice the two most important cases are R = Z and R = Z2. This determines whether a fundamental (orientation) class with coefficients in R can exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of H_n(M;R) and fundamental class existence (Theorem 3.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed connected n-manifold M: (a) If M is R-orientable, H_n(M;R) → H_n(M||x;R) ≈ R is an isomorphism for all x. (b) If M is not R-orientable, the map is injective with image {r ∈ R | 2r = 0}. (c) H_i(M;R) = 0 for i > n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular H_n(M;Z) is Z or 0 depending on orientability, and H_n(M;Z2)=Z2. An element whose image in each local H_n(M||x;R) is a generator is called a fundamental (orientation) class; existence implies M is closed and R-orientable and conversely. Theorem follows from the more technical Lemma 3.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global uniqueness/existence and vanishing (Lemma 3.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For manifold M of dimension n and compact A ⊂ M: (a) any section x ↦ α_x of the covering MR→M comes from a unique class α_A ∈ H_n(M||A;R) whose image in H_n(M||x;R) is α_x for all x∈A. (b) H_i(M||A;R)=0 for i>n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by Mayer–Vietoris and reduction to the case A ⊂ R^n (convex), then an argument using relative cycles and coverings by balls. Lemma is the technical engine for Theorem 3.26 and many vanishing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and characterization of a fundamental (orientation) class
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundamental class for M with coefficients in R is an element of H_n(M;R) whose image in H_n(M||x;R) is a generator for every x∈M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence ⇔ M closed and R-orientable. A fundamental class may also be called an orientation class; representatives in simplicial homology must have coefficients ±1 on top simplices (for Z-coefficients) and sign choices correspond to orientability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit simplicial construction of fundamental class (simplicial manifolds)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed n-manifold with a simplicial structure, a Z fundamental class is represented by a linear combination ∑ k_i σ_i of the n-simplices where each coefficient k_i = ±1 and the sum is a cycle. A choice of signs making ∑ k_i σ_i a cycle exists iff M is orientable; for Z2 coefficients ∑ σ_i always defines a fundamental class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete combinatorial criterion for orientability and for constructing an orientation class in the simplicial setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of high-dimensional homology for noncompact manifolds (Proposition 3.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a connected noncompact n-manifold then H_i(M;R)=0 for i≥n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: represent classes by cycles with compact image, place them in an open set with compact closure and use long exact sequences and Lemma 3.27. For i=n classes define sections of MR; compact support forces them to vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of cap product
rubrics_metrics.description: The cap product is an R-bilinear pairing C_k(X;R) × C^ℓ(X;R) → C_{k-ℓ}(X;R) (for k≥ℓ) defined on a simplex σ by σ ⌢ ϕ = ϕ(σ||[v_0,...,v_ℓ]) · σ||[v_ℓ,...,v_k], inducing H_k × H^ℓ → H_{k-ℓ}. It satisfies ∂(σ⌢ϕ) = (−1)^ℓ(∂σ⌢ϕ − σ⌢δϕ) so cycles/cocycles pair to cycles, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cap product has relative versions H_k(X,A) × H^ℓ(X) → H_{k-ℓ}(X,A) and more general relative forms. Naturality formula (informal): f_*(α) ⌢ ϕ = f_*(α ⌢ f^*(ϕ)). Cap product is R-linear in each variable and interacts with cup product via ψ(α⌢ϕ) = (ϕ ∪ ψ)(α).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology with compact supports (definition and direct-limit description)
rubrics_metrics.description: C^i_c(X;G) are cochains ϕ such that ϕ vanishes on chains in X − K for some compact K (depending on ϕ); H^i_c(X;G) is the cohomology of that subcomplex. Equivalently H^i_c(X;G) ≅ lim_{K compact} H^i(X,X−K;G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative, stronger notions of 'compact support' for cochains do not form subcomplexes. Example: H^n_c(R^n;G) ≈ G and H^i_c(R^n;G)=0 for i≠n. Proper maps induce maps on H^*_c; cohomology with compact supports is not a homotopy invariant in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality map for noncompact manifolds (construction via compact supports)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-orientable n-manifold M (possibly noncompact) define DM: H^k_c(M;R) → H_{n-k}(M;R) in the limit by using, for each compact K⊂M, the unique µ_K ∈ H_n(M||K;R) orienting K, and the cap product maps H^k(M||K;R) → H_{n-k}(M;R); these assemble to yield DM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the natural generalization of Poincaré duality for the noncompact case, relying on Lemma 3.27 for uniqueness of µ_K and on passage to direct limits over compact subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré Duality for closed manifolds (Theorem 3.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a closed R-orientable n-manifold with fundamental class [M] ∈ H_n(M;R), then D : H^k(M;R) → H_{n-k}(M;R) defined by D(α) = [M] ⌢ α is an isomorphism for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses properties of cap product, Mayer–Vietoris induction, and the technical lemmas about local classes and compact supports. Existence of [M] follows from Theorem 3.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré Duality for general R-orientable manifolds (Theorem 3.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-orientable n-manifold M (not necessarily compact), the duality map DM : H^k_c(M;R) → H_{n-k}(M;R) is an isomorphism for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: reduce to the R^n case, then to open subsets of R^n, use Mayer–Vietoris induction and direct-limit arguments over nested unions of open sets; a technical Mayer–Vietoris commutativity lemma (Lemma 3.36) is required to pass to limits correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayer–Vietoris technical commutative diagram (Lemma 3.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M = U ∪ V are open, there is a diagram of Mayer–Vietoris sequences (cohomology with compact supports vs homology) that commutes up to sign; passing to limits over compact subsets yields the Mayer–Vietoris diagram used in the induction step for duality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof checks commutativity on cycles/cocycles for the non-boundary squares and handles the delicate square involving coboundary/boundary using explicit chain representatives and sign bookkeeping; this technical commutativity is essential to apply the five-lemma after passing to direct limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary on torsion in H_{n-1}(M;Z) (Corollary 3.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: For closed connected n-manifold M, the torsion subgroup of H_{n-1}(M;Z) is trivial if M is orientable and Z2 if M is nonorientable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses the universal coefficient theorem and computations of H_n(M;Z_p) for primes p; the Z2 torsion in the nonorientable case arises from the Bockstein image from H_n(M;Z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler characteristic vanishing in odd dimensions (Corollary 3.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed manifold of odd dimension has Euler characteristic zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: Poincaré duality pairs H^i and H^{n-i}, giving equal ranks; in odd n these ranks cancel in the alternating sum. For nonorientable case use Z2 coefficients and the universal coefficient theorem to compare contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cup–cap relationship and nonsingularity of the cup pairing (Proposition 3.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cup and cap are related by ψ(α ⌢ ϕ) = (ϕ ∪ ψ)(α). For a closed R-orientable n-manifold the cup product pairing H^k × H^{n-k} → R, (ϕ,ψ) ↦ (ϕ ∪ ψ)[M], is nonsingular when R is a field or when R=Z and torsion is factored out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: consider composition H^{n-k} → Hom_R(H_{n-k},R) → Hom_R(H^k,R) where the second map is dual to Poincaré duality; when the universal coefficient map h is an iso (fields or torsion-free integer case) this shows nonsingularity. Consequence: cup product detects infinite cyclic summands (see Corollary 3.39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for generating infinite cyclic summands via cup product (Corollary 3.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: For closed connected orientable n-manifold M, α ∈ H^k(M;Z) generates an infinite cyclic summand of H^k(M;Z) iff there exists β ∈ H^{n-k}(M;Z) with α ∪ β a generator of H^n(M;Z) ≈ Z. Over a field, any nonzero α has such a β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from nonsingularity of the cup pairing and Poincaré duality; it gives a usable test for detecting free rank in cohomology via cup products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation examples and checks (surfaces and R^n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples showing Poincaré duality in action: closed orientable surface of genus g — explicit simplicial fundamental class and cap products that identify Poincaré duals of standard H_1/H^1 generators; nonorientable surfaces use Z2 coefficients. For R^n, H^n_c(R^n;G) ≈ G and the duality map is cap product with a relative generator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples serve as sanity checks and models for the general proofs: R^n is the local model used in Mayer–Vietoris induction; surfaces afford explicit simplicial calculations illustrating signs and Z vs Z2 phenomena.
